title: Host copy consolidation and threadpool smoothing to reduce prefill/decode overhead
creator: Priya Patel
description: Background: Our production traces and perf dashboards show repeated short-lived host->device memcpy bursts and frequent threadpool wakeups during prefill and decode phases for small/medium batch traces. These generate tail latency spikes (p95/p99) and elevated host CPU usage for multi-tenant Dedicated clusters. Goal: Introduce a compact host-side consolidation layer plus a threadpool smoothing strategy and lightweight kernel classifier so that small-batch requests are coalesced with minimal added latency and the runtime chooses lower-overhead kernels when beneficial. The overall aim is to reduce CPU overhead, lower memcpy counts, and improve p50/p95 latency without degrading throughput or model quality.
proposed_solution: 1) Copy Consolidation Service: a per-device bounded queue that coalesces proximate memcpy requests (same device, same direction) within a short time window (configurable jitter ~50-150us) and emits a single batched DMA operation with offsets. 2) Threadpool Smoothing (ThreadPark): instead of immediate worker wake per job, use a short park-and-batch window to reduce wakeups for microsubmissions while respecting latency SLOs. 3) Kernel Classifier: a lightweight prober that selects between 'fast-small' and 'fast-large' kernel variants based on predicted effective tokens per request and current device load. 4) Attention micro-fuse: apply selective attention kernel fusing (rotary + qkv pack) only when kernel-classifier predicts throughput wins for small sequence lengths. 5) Telemetry hooks: add counters for consolidated-memcpy-count, thread-wake-rate, kernel-decisions, and consolidated-copy-size distribution.
design_decisions: Use conservative default coalescing window (100us) with per-customer override to avoid cross-customer data mixing in Dedicated; coalescing is per-vm/pool to preserve isolation.
Prefer non-blocking ring buffer for the consolidation queue to avoid head-of-line blocking; fall back to direct memcpy when queue is full and request is latency-sensitive.
ThreadPark default timeout 80us; adaptively shorten on high-traffic devices using a moving-average latency signal.
Kernel classifier runs asynchronously and updates a shared hint; full kernel switch only occurs at safe scheduling points to avoid preemption complexity.
Attention micro-fuse is gated behind model-compatibility checks and model-verified accuracy regression tests.
Expose knobs in console (runtime-1.25) for coalescing-window, threadpark-ms, and kernel-hint-policy for experiments.
Fail-open behavior: if consolidation module reports errors, route to legacy path to avoid customer impact.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for 1-4 batch size prefill requests decreases by >=15% on median Dedicated hosts compared to baseline without consolidation (measured on runtime-1.24 config)
Host CPU utilization during steady-state small-batch workload reduces by >=20% for the consolidation-enabled hosts
Memcopy operation count (host->device) per 1M tokens decreases by >=25% on coalescing hosts
No regression in model outputs: automated evals show <0.05% delta in end-to-end token perplexity for affected models
Feature flags to toggle consolidation and threadpark are present and respected at runtime (canary rollout path defined)
End-to-end canary run on production-like Dedicated pool shows no SLO violations for 24h before >=50% rollout
tasks: Spike: microbench copy consolidation latency/overhead (PR: gh/runtime#1789)
Implement ThreadPark in worker scheduler with adaptive timeout policy
Add kernel classifier and small-batch kernel path; instrument decision telemetry
Integrate attention micro-fuse pass into kernel selection flow (with model compatibility checks)
Add metrics and dashboards: consolidated-copy-rate, thread-wake-rate, kernel-hint-signal
E2E benchmarks: run 1B token hybrid workload comparing runtime-1.24 vs runtime-1.25
PR reviews, load-testing in staging, security review (if needed), canary rollout
metrics: p50/p95/p99 prefill latency by batch size
Host CPU user/system % during prefill/decode windows
Number of host->device memcpy ops per 1M tokens
Average consolidated batch size (bytes and ops)
Thread wakeups per second per device
rollout_plan: Feature flag off in prod (default). Merge to main behind feature flag.
Canary 5% of Dedicated pool with conservative coalesce window; monitor metrics for 24h
If stable, expand to 25% and enable ThreadPark; run regression evals
50% rollout for regional pools while keeping user isolation boundaries; run chaos tests
Full rollout after 72h with no regressions and metrics targets met
Provide rollback knob to disable consolidation at pool level instantly
testing_plan: Unit tests for aggregation logic (edge cases: full queue, partial gaps)
Integration tests with GPU emulator to validate offset/stride correctness
Performance microbench against representative models (long-form and chat)
Deterministic eval runs to ensure attention-fuse does not change outputs beyond threshold
Staging soak with synthetic small-batch traffic and real customer traces anonymized
notes: Tradeoffs: larger coalescing windows improve memcpy savings but increase per-request latency; default aims to capture nearby microsubmissions without hurting SLOs.
This ticket intentionally separates consolidation from persistent KV caching; both can be complementary but KV cache changes left to follow-up.
We must coordinate with Dedicated provisioning team to ensure per-device queues do not exhaust memory in multi-tenant scenarios.
Related work: kernel selector tuning from ENG-30112 and threadpool improvements in ENG-72018 should be reconciled during integration.
